name: Zimri
overview: Zimri was a male member of the tribe of Simeon known primarily as the man pierced by Phinehas, an event recorded in Numbers 25:14. This distinct act marks him as a significant figure within the narrative, though further personal details are not provided. His role is noted without additional commentary or elaboration in the biblical text.
namesAndTitles: The name Zimri means 'wild goats, sheep; possibly awe of YHWH' in Hebrew. This proper name does not appear to have been given directly by God but reflects common naming conventions of the time, possibly indicating traits or attributes valued in the culture.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture records that Zimri was the father of Salu, as explicitly stated in Numbers 25:14. Beyond this, no other family relationships are detailed in the biblical account.
scriptureSignificance: Zimri's significance in the biblical narrative centers on his confrontation with Phinehas, which is emblematic of zeal for God's holiness and judgment against sin. His death by Phinehas's hand underscores the seriousness of Israel's covenant faithfulness and the consequences of disobedience. This incident highlights the tension between divine justice and communal purity within Israel's history.
